prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset: one production transparent sprite for a 144px-wide isometric grid game.
Redraw the teal manual metalworking lathe in reference 1 from scratch, correcting its toy-like oversized feet, oversized controls, oversized headstock, and floor-level working bed. References 2 (factory desk) and 3 (private cache) set the EXACT approved hand-painted game art style; reference 4 sets the ground rectangle and camera. Replace the geometry of reference 1, retaining only its recognisable lathe subject and muted teal / cream repaired industrial palette.

GEOMETRY: a long narrow 2-by-1-cell lathe, viewed orthographically from above, long axis from upper-left to lower-right. Native ground axes have slopes +0.7071 and -0.7071 as in reference 4. Vertical edges stay vertical, no convergence. Correct lathe construction: slender long steel bed raised to a standing person's WAIST, supported by TWO modest upright cabinet pedestals under its ends, with an open space beneath the middle of the bed. Compact headstock on the upper-left end rises only to a person's chest; matching small tailstock at lower-right. Three-jaw chuck and tailstock center share a single straight spindle axis. A modest carriage and small toolpost ride the bed. Small handwheels and short handles fit a human hand, not a human torso. Simple apron and lead screw on the visible near side. Main bed length is clearly longer than headstock width, balanced practical workshop proportions. Ground depth is one cell, length two cells, not a massive broad 3-by-2 machine. Four compact feet integrated into the two narrow cabinets; NO massive plinths. Cabinet/bed support height should read as a normal standing workbench, not flat or ground-mounted.

STYLE: exactly the friendly but substantial hand-painted, ink-outlined room props in references 2 and 3: dark variable-weight outer contour, broad readable painted planes, simple restrained inner lines, warm upper-left lighting. Muted worn teal paint, one cream replacement access panel, localized chipped corners, oily touches close to moving parts, a few repair bolts. A used and repaired working machine in a modern salvage settlement. Keep wear selective and silhouette very legible at about 200 pixels on screen. Avoid noisy tiny machinery details or photo-real/PBR/3D render highlights.

OUTPUT: only ONE complete lathe, centered with padding on a genuinely transparent background. Native correct proportions and camera, no stretching required. No grid, no reference mat, no floor, no cast shadow or ambient halo, no platform/base plate, no person, no accessories around it, no lettering, no labels, no checkerboard. The geometry reference itself must not appear in the output.
